entities.name: war on terror
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The War on Terror, a military campaign initiated in response to the September 11 attacks, was a pivotal event in global history. It began on September 11, 2001, with the coordinated terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center in New York City and the Pentagon in Washington, D.C., resulting in nearly 3,000 deaths. The subsequent US-led military operations in Afghanistan and Iraq, which lasted until August 30, 2021, had far-reaching consequences, including the displacement of millions of people, the deaths of thousands of soldiers and civilians, and a significant escalation of global terrorism. The War on Terror also marked a significant turning point in the history of the Middle East, as it led to the overthrow of governments in Afghanistan and Iraq, and contributed to the rise of extremist groups like ISIS.

The War on Terror was a response to the threat posed by Al-Qaeda, a terrorist organization led by Osama bin Laden, which had declared war on the United States and its allies. The campaign involved a complex interplay of military, intelligence, and diplomatic efforts, as well as a significant expansion of US military presence in the Middle East and South Asia. The War on Terror also had significant domestic and international implications, including the passage of the USA PATRIOT Act, the establishment of the Department of Homeland Security, and a significant increase in global military spending.

The War on Terror had a lasting impact on global politics, economies, and societies, shaping the trajectory of international relations, global security, and human rights. As the world continues to grapple with the consequences of this event, it serves as a powerful reminder of the complexities and challenges of modern global politics.
